## Human Revision

### Statement

For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, define $a_n = \frac{n-1}{n}$. Prove each as true or false. Rewrite statements using $\forall$ and $\exists$.

1. For each real number $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for evvery $n \in \mathbb{N}$, if $n > N$ then $|a_n - 0| < \varepsilon$.

1. For each real number $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for evvery $n \in \mathbb{N}$, if $n > N$ then $|a_n - 1| < \varepsilon$.

### Solution

1. Rewritten: $\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}$, if $n > N$ then $|a_n - 0| < \varepsilon$.

<!-- If true, let $\varepsilon > 0$.
Let $N = ____$.
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Suppose $n > N$.
We compute
\begin{align*}
|a_n - 0| &= |a_n|\\
&= \left|\frac{n-1}{n}\right|\\
&\ \vdots \quad  \text{(fill in gap)}\\
&< \varepsilon.
\end{align*} -->

If false, $\exists \varepsilon > 0$ s.t. $\forall N \in \mathbb{N}$, $\exists n\in \mathbb{N}$ s.t. $n > N$ and $|a_n - 0| \ge \varepsilon$.

Let $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2}$.
Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
Let $n = 1 + N$.
We compute $n = 1+N > N$.
We compute
\begin{align*}
|a_n - 0| &= \left|\frac{n-1}{n}\right|\\
&= \frac{n-1}{n} &(n \ge 1)\\
&= 1 - \frac{1}{n}\\
&= 1 - \frac{1}{1+N}
&\ge 1 - \frac{1}{2}\\
&= \frac{1}{2}\\
&= \varepsilon.
\end{align*}

(Start of part 2 courtesy of Bro. Woodruff and Kennedy)

2. $\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists N \in \mathbb{N}$ s.t. $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}$, if $n > N$, then $|a_n -1| < \varepsilon$.

Let $\varepsilon > 0$.
Use the Archimedean property to pick $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $N > \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$.
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Suppose $n > N$.
We compute
\begin{align*}
|a_n -1| &= \left| \frac{n-1}{n} - 1\right| &\text{(substitute)}\\
&= \left| \frac{n}{n} - \frac{1}{n} - 1 \right|\\
&= \left| -\frac{1}{n} \right|\\
&= \frac{1}{n}\\
&< \frac{1}{N} &(n > N \text{ so } \frac{1}{n} < \frac{1}{N})\\
&< \varepsilon. &(N > \frac{1}{\varepsilon} \text{ so } \varepsilon > \frac{1}{N})
\end{align*}
$\square$

### Solution

1. $\forall \mathbb{R}\ \epsilon > 0$, $\exists N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}$, if $n > N$ then $|a_n - 0| < \epsilon$.

True

Let $\epsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\epsilon > 0$.
Let $N =$.
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_n = \frac{n-1}{n}$.
Suppose $n > N$.

We compute $a_n = \frac{n-1}{n}$.
We then know $1 > a_n > 0$.
Then by inequality property we can substitute to get the expression $1 - 0 > a_n - 0 > 0 - 0$ which is equivalent to $1 > a_n - 0 > 0$.
Then by the absolute value property we know $|1| > |a_n - 0| > |0|$ is equivalent to $1 > |a_n - 0| > 0$.

$0.11$

$\frac{10}{11}\quad \frac{1}{2}$

$0.5\quad n+1$

Negation: $\exists \mathbb{R}\ \epsilon > 0$ such that $\forall N \in \mathbb{N}$, $\exists n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $n > N$ and $|a_n - 1| \geq \epsilon$.

False

Let $\epsilon = 0.25$.
Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $n = N+1$ such that $a_n = \frac{n-1}{n}$.
Because $n = N+1$ by property we know $n > N$.
Because $n = N+1$ and $a_n = \frac{n-1}{n}$, by substitution we know $a_{N+1} = \frac{N+1-1}{N+1}$ which is equivalent to $a_{N+1} = \frac{N}{N+1}$.
Note $a_n = a_{N+1}$.
We compute
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_n - 1 &= \frac{N}{N+1} - 1,\\
&= \frac{N}{N+1} - \frac{N+1}{N+1}\\
a_n - 1 &= \frac{-1}{N+1}
\end{aligned}
$$
